rules.name: web and server meet only in shared
rules.why: The web page runs in the browser and the server runs in Node; code one imports from the other drags the wrong runtime in and ties the browser fallback to server internals.
rules.fix: Put the type or pure helper both sides need in shared/ and import it from there; anything else stays on its own side and travels over the HTTP API.

rules.name: shared imports only shared
rules.why: shared/ is loaded by both the browser page and the Node server, so it can depend on nothing that only one of them has: no server or web file, no Node built-in, no package.
rules.fix: Keep shared/ to types and plain data or functions that import only other shared/ files; put code that needs Node in server/ and code that needs the browser in web/.

rules.name: Windows web view stays in its adapter
rules.why: Windows is a desktop-only test build: flutter/lib/windows_web_view.dart puts WebView2 behind the webview_flutter interface so the rest of the client, and later Android, stay free of Windows code.
rules.fix: Add the Windows call to flutter/lib/windows_web_view.dart behind the webview_flutter interface the rest of the client already uses.
